transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in because I just can’t shake this feeling that everything that goes wrong is my fault. Like at work I feel like I’m a bad employee, and at home I feel like I’m failing there too… like I’m a bad homeowner and I somehow deserve to lose the things I worked for. It’s been hard to get away from that.
Have you noticed that you don’t enjoy things as much as you used to, or that it’s hard to get interested in activities you used to like?

Yeah. I used to actually look forward to things, like planning brunch with friends, painting in my spare room, going hiking, or signing up for networking events. Now it all just feels like chores, or like I’m pretending to care because I know I’m supposed to.
Have you been feeling like you’re not good enough or that you’re a failure more days than not?

Yes. More days than not I feel like I’m not good enough. If something goes wrong, I immediately think it’s my fault. At work I feel like I’m a bad employee, and at home I feel like I’m failing too… like I don’t deserve to keep what I’ve worked for.
Have you been feeling this way most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row?

Yes… it’s been most days, and it takes up a lot of the day. I keep getting stuck on the idea that if something goes wrong, it’s because of me. Like I’m failing at work, failing at home, and I don’t deserve what I’ve worked for.
Have you had days where you felt down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, rather than just feeling like a failure or guilty?
Yes. It’s been more than just guilt. I’ve felt depressed and uninterested in things for… about two years and one month now. It’s there most of the time.
Have there been any periods lasting at least a few weeks where your mood improved significantly, even if just briefly, during these two years?

Yes, there was a stretch for a few weeks where my mood felt lighter. I was getting through work more normally, not feeling quite as weighed down. But even then, I was still hearing the voice near the vents, and I still believed the mortgage company and my coworkers were monitoring me.

Can you tell me more about hearing voices near the vents and believing the mortgage company and your coworkers were monitoring you? Were these thoughts something you were sure were true even when others said they weren’t real?

Yes. Even on days when my mood is a little better, I still feel sure the mortgage company and people at work are watching me. Like they’re looking for mistakes so they can show I’m irresponsible and take my townhouse from me. Other people tell me that doesn’t make sense, but it still feels true to me.
Do you believe these things about being monitored and that your coworkers and the mortgage company are trying to take your house, even when there’s no evidence to support that?

Yes. Even when I’m having an okay day, I still feel convinced they’re watching me—like the mortgage company and people at work are waiting for me to mess up so they can say I’m irresponsible and take my townhouse. I know other people don’t see evidence for it, but it still feels real to me.
